title: Point-to-Point vs. Hub Integration Cost
description: Move one slider and watch point-to-point connections grow as N(N-1)/2 while hub connections grow as N.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Data Management and Governance

educational.learningObjective: Given a number of systems needing to exchange data, the learner will calculate the number of connections required under a point-to-point architecture versus a hub architecture, and explain why the hub scales better.
prerequisites: Knows what a system integration is
learningOutcomes: Calculate the connection count for both architectures at a given N
Explain why quadratic growth makes point-to-point unmanageable
Recognize the hub pattern when it appears in other contexts
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Ask learners to compute both counts for N = 12 without the slider, then check.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Single-slider side-by-side comparison with live formula readouts
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Scale variation to make an arithmetic difference undeniable
pedagogical.feedbackType: Both diagrams and both counts redraw continuously as the slider moves
misconceptionsAddressed: That point-to-point integration scales acceptably with careful engineering
That the hub's advantage is about technology rather than about counting
discussionQuestions: What does the hub cost that point-to-point does not?
Why do organizations end up with point-to-point integration even when they know the arithmetic?
Where else does this same N-versus-N-squared pattern show up?
